mcqs.learning_point: Use multiplication to obtain equivalent fractions
mcqs.question: Which of the following fractions is equivalent to \(\frac{2}{5}\) obtained by multiplying the numerator and denominator by the same whole number?
mcqs.explanation: Multiplying both numerator and denominator of \(\frac{2}{5}\) by 2 gives \(\frac{2\times2}{5\times2}=\frac{4}{10}\). Options B, C and D are not obtained by such multiplication and are not equivalent to \(\frac{2}{5}\).

mcqs.question: Which fraction, when both its numerator and denominator are divided by the same integer, reduces to \(\frac{3}{4}\)?
mcqs.explanation: Dividing numerator and denominator of \(\frac{9}{12}\) by 3 gives \(\frac{9\div3}{12\div3}=\frac{3}{4}\). The other options do not simplify to \(\frac{3}{4}\) with a single common divisor.

mcqs.question: Identify the fraction that is NOT in its simplest form.
mcqs.explanation: Both 14 and 21 share a common factor of 7; dividing by 7 gives \(\frac{2}{3}\). Hence \(\frac{14}{21}\) is not in simplest form. The other fractions have no common factor other than 1.

mcqs.learning_point: Explain why equivalent fractions represent the same quantity
mcqs.question: Which statement best explains why \(\frac{3}{6}\) and \(\frac{1}{2}\) represent the same quantity?

options.A: Both fractions have the same numerator.
options.B: Both fractions have the same denominator.
options.C: Both fractions can be reduced to the same simplest form.

mcqs.answer: Both fractions can be reduced to the same simplest form.
mcqs.explanation: Dividing numerator and denominator of \(\frac{3}{6}\) by 3 gives \(\frac{1}{2}\). Thus they reduce to the same simplest form, meaning they represent the same part of a whole. Options A and B are false, and D is incorrect because both fractions are proper.
